extracted.intended_audience: people (developers/makers/writers) who want to post submissions on Hacker News
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, tactical guidance for submitting links/posts to Hacker News (Show HN / Ask HN / general submissions) to avoid flags, maximize engagement, and encourage organic discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't share direct links for upvotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not share the direct HN post link on Slack/Discord/etc. and ask people to upvote—those votes won't count and may trigger vote-ring detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN’s algorithm ignores such votes and may penalize the post. Instead, aim to spark organic discussion (comments boost ranking). If friends/family will help, they must manually find your post on HN (/newest, /show, or the chosen category) rather than clicking a direct shared link for upvotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't ask for upvotes or use sockpuppet accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly asking for upvotes or using multiple accounts to manipulate votes is prohibited and will get your post flagged or your account banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play fair and let the community decide. Both behaviour types are considered vote manipulation and are enforced against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific, descriptive titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose clear, specific titles that summarize the contribution (e.g., 'How we reduced API latency by 90%' vs. 'Improving performance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clickbait, ALL CAPS, or excessive punctuation. HN users value clarity and professionalism—your title is your first impression and strongly affects engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post during peak hours (9 AM–12 PM Pacific Time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing affects visibility; post when most users are active—commonly 9 AM–12 PM Pacific Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid weekends and late nights (Pacific Time equivalent) as engagement tends to drop then. Community observations indicate peak-morning posting increases chances of traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose affiliations transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are sharing your own work, clearly disclose that affiliation in the title or post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles like 'Show HN: My open-source tool for X' or 'I built a new database' are acceptable. Hiding affiliation will backfire—HN values transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage organic discussion in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster and prioritize comments because discussions are a stronger ranking signal than raw upvotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to engage with thoughtful responses; if someone critiques your post, reply with data or reasoning rather than defensiveness. Prompting substantive conversation helps ranking more than soliciting votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include technical details and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide substantive content—code snippets, benchmarks, architecture diagrams, deep dives—rather than shallow marketing copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN users favor detailed, technical posts. If your submission reads like a press release or marketing fluff, it will likely be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't repost the same content
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid reposting identical links; HN’s duplicate detection is robust and reposts can be flagged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a post failed, wait a few weeks and try again with a new angle or title rather than reposting the same content immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage respectfully in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain civility and thoughtful tone in discussions; respectful engagement builds credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If someone is hostile, don’t escalate—report abuse if necessary. Thoughtful responses are rewarded; antagonistic behavior harms reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage 'Show HN' and 'Ask HN' correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use site-specific tags/features appropriately: 'Show HN' for showcasing polished projects and 'Ask HN' for substantive questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misusing these (e.g., posting unfinished projects as Show HN or trivial questions as Ask HN) leads to disinterest. Match the tag to the content and audience expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write concise, scannable content
rubrics_metrics.description: Format your post so HN users can quickly scan key points: use bullet points, subheadings, and short paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many users skim; make key insights easy to find. Concise, well-structured text increases readability and likelihood of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor HN’s 'new' page and engage with others' posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively participate on the platform by viewing and engaging with new posts to build goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upvoting and commenting on others’ posts is a long-term strategy that can pay off. Do not spam comments solely to gain visibility—engage genuinely where you have something to add.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid editing titles after posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from changing your post title after submission because the algorithm may penalize edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose your title carefully before submitting to avoid potential ranking penalties for post-title edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage HN's 'second chance' system
rubrics_metrics.description: If a post fails to gain traction, moderators may give it a second chance instead of deleting it immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t delete a post too quickly; check the /pool for second-chance posts. High-quality content might be revived by moderators if it merits another look.
